newsitem.title: UK: BAA agrees new deal with Nuance.
newsitem.headline: BAA agrees new deal with Nuance.

text.p: British airports company BAA Plc said on Tuesday it had completed a renegotiation of a number of contracts under which Swiss airline group Swissair's Nuance unit manages some BAA duty and tax-free shops.

"From spring 1997, the contracts to manage shops in Heathrow terminal 2, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Aberdeen, Stansted and Southampton will cease," BAA said in a statement, adding that these had been due to expire in June 1999.
Nuance acquired the BAA contracts as part of its acquisition of Allders Plc unit Allders International in July.
It will continue to manage large BAA shops in Heathrow terminal 4 and Gatwick south terminal which BAA said "represent a significant part of their existing business with BAA".
Group retail director Barry Gibson said BAA's moves were part of a clearly-established strategic aim to win a significant position in the international retail market.

"We took the decision (some time ago) to take more control of our duty and tax free business as the first step, and we are now implementing that decision. We remain interested in pursuing opportunities to develop our business," he added.
